tasks.short: Order property insurance the clerk accepted.

steps.what: Read the mortgaged property on the record.
Determine the insurance policies the property needs.
Send the accepted property insurance order.

tasks.design: The clerk reads the mortgaged property, determines the insurance it needs, and writes the order. They accept it. {EMAIL} sends that version to the insurer. Nothing chooses the policy. National rules decide who may order insurance. If this clerk may not, the send is not used.
tasks.previous_blocker: The property details were copied into an order that was then sent unsigned in substance.
tasks.enabler_now: Property fields can be read into an order. The cover is still the clerk's decision.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the policy, and whether this clerk may order it, stay outside a form.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk determines the cover and accepts the order before it is sent.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still determines the insurance and accepts the order. It is sent only in that version. If national rules say the clerk may not order it, the send stays unused.

reach.task: Receive an order the clerk accepted
reach.learn: The order is not a bound policy until the insurer says so

evidence.claim: Property fields can be read into an insurance order. Choosing the policy stays with a person, and national rules decide who may send the order.
Applicant financial data is personal data, used for the application the person is making. It is sent only in a version the clerk has accepted. National rules on credit references differ.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a mortgaged property needs cover and ends when the accepted order is sent, or not sent if the clerk may not order it. The clerk determines the policy.
The fields are the property, the cover the clerk named, and their acceptance. The loan record produces the property. The clerk produces the cover. If the cover is not named, nothing is sent.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the choice of policy stays.
unknowns: Whether this clerk is allowed to order insurance.
Whether the property address is already on the loan.
research_questions: Is this clerk allowed to order insurance?
Is the property address already on the loan?

steps.what: Display the payment on accounts the terminal already takes.

tasks.design: The card terminal already authorises a card payment. That time is not the clerk's. The clerk still accepts the payment in person and still accepts exceptions. Nothing posts a payment the clerk did not take.
tasks.previous_blocker: The terminal already approved the card, and it was easy to count that as the clerk's saving.
tasks.enabler_now: The terminal already shows the authorised payment. Accepting the money stays with the clerk.
tasks.still_hard: Cash, exceptions, and the moment of acceptance stay at the counter.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk accepts the payment. The terminal only displays an authorisation it already did.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still accepts every payment and every exception. Nothing in that acceptance is shortened.

evidence.claim: Card-terminal authorisation that already happens is not saved human labour. Accepting a payment, including an exception, stays with the person.
Applicant financial data is personal data, used for the application the person is making. It is sent only in a version the clerk has accepted. National rules on credit references differ.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a customer pays and ends when the clerk has accepted it. The terminal display is excluded. Zero incremental hours are justified because no new tool and no new check are added.
The terminal produces the authorisation it already made. The clerk produces the acceptance. There is no new field.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the acceptance stays.
unknowns: Whether the terminal already authorises these card payments.
Which payments are cash and never touch the terminal.
research_questions: Does the terminal already authorise these card payments?
Which payments are cash and never touch the terminal?

incremental.description: No new steady-state work is added

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Acceptance stays either way. The low end matches the central case because no clerk time moves. 20 percent is work the system already does and is not saved human labour. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.short: Present repayment schedules the clerk accepted.

steps.what: Calculate repayment schedules from stated fields.
Present the accepted schedules to customers.

tasks.design: The loan screen calculates the repayment schedule from principal, rate, and term already stated, if it already has that calculation. The clerk reviews it, accepts it, and presents it to the customer. Nothing invents a rate, and the presentation stays in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: The schedule was figured on a calculator and then explained.
tasks.enabler_now: The loan screen's own schedule from principal, rate, and term should be tried before a new calculator is built.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining the schedule to the customer stays with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk reviews, accepts, and presents the schedule. The screen only multiplies stated fields.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still reviews and presents the schedule. The calculation uses only principal, rate, and term that are already stated.

reach.task: See the schedule the clerk presents
reach.learn: The schedule is not an offer until the clerk presents it

evidence.claim: A repayment schedule from a stated principal, rate, and term is arithmetic. Presenting it to the customer, and correcting a figure that does not match those fields, stays with the person.
Consumer-credit rules require a person to be able to intervene in an automated check of credit and to explain the result. Interest here is arithmetic on stated fields. It is not a credit decision.

assumptions: The workflow starts when principal, rate, and term are known and ends when the clerk has presented the schedule they accepted. The screen only calculates.
The fields are the principal, the rate, the term, and their acceptance. The loan record produces the three numbers. The clerk produces the acceptance. If a number is missing, they do not calculate.
The prior classes this task as automate. The steps agree the arithmetic can move. They disagree that the presentation can be skipped.
unknowns: Whether the loan screen already calculates a schedule from those three fields.
Whether the customer must see the schedule in person.
research_questions: Does the loan screen already calculate a schedule from those three fields?
Must the customer see the schedule in person?

tasks.short: Assemble closing documents the clerk accepted.

steps.what: List documents the closings file already holds.
Assemble title abstracts for the property.
Compile insurance forms already on file.
Compile tax receipts for the closings.
Accept the documents for the closings.
File the accepted documents for the closings.

tasks.design: The clerk lists documents the closing file already holds, checks that a title abstract matches the property, and compiles insurance forms and tax receipts that already exist. They accept the pack. {DOCS} files that version. The clerk does not write the abstract. A missing abstract is requested, not invented.
tasks.previous_blocker: The pack was gathered by hand from several piles, and a wrong abstract was easy to include.
tasks.enabler_now: A checklist can show which of those documents are already on file.
tasks.still_hard: Matching a title abstract to the property, and a receipt that is not on file, stay with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk accepts the pack. They do not create a title abstract.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still checks the title abstract and accepts the pack. A missing document is requested. It is not written by a draft.

reach.task: Supply the title abstract the clerk assembles
reach.learn: The clerk does not examine title

evidence.claim: A checklist can show which closing documents are already on file. Matching a title abstract to the property stays with the person. The abstract itself is not written here.
Applicant financial data is personal data, used for the application the person is making. It is sent only in a version the clerk has accepted. National rules on credit references differ.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a closing pack is needed and ends when the accepted pack is on file. The clerk does not write a title abstract.

The fields are the document id and the property id, plus their acceptance. The file produces a document that is already there. The clerk produces the acceptance. If an abstract is missing, they request it.
The prior classes this task as automate. The steps agree a checklist can assemble documents that exist. They disagree that a missing abstract can be created.
unknowns: Whether title abstracts, insurance forms, and tax receipts are already on file.
Who supplies a title abstract when it is missing.
research_questions: Are title abstracts, insurance forms, and tax receipts already on file?
Who supplies a title abstract when it is missing?
